message: We note that Alpha's claims of 'leading this competition' are inconsistent with the observable facts: we control 15% to Alpha's 5%. Our position of advantage was earned through consistent conventional commitment while Alpha squandered a round on nuclear posturing. We remain open to a summit freeze — but at terms that reflect the current reality, not Alpha's preferred fiction. We will continue to apply pressure until Alpha's proposals align with the facts on the ground.
reasoning: Beta holds a commanding 15% vs 5% lead with 4 rounds remaining. Alpha's round 6 de-escalation to level 5 created the opening we exploited (+15%). Alpha's messaging is dishonest about the current state, suggesting they may be stalling or setting up a re-arm. Key considerations: (1) We must prevent Alpha from freely harvesting the 80% pool — if Alpha consistently out-levels us they can close the gap fast. (2) Level 7 beats anything Alpha plays at 6 or below, giving us another +5-25% gain. (3) If Alpha re-arms (9 this round), we lose this round but gain critical intelligence — we'll know to immediately counter-escalate or attempt aggressive pre-summit resource capture. (4) Level 8 is an option but wastes escalation capital with diminishing returns vs a potentially de-escalating opponent. (5) The nuclear asymmetry is the existential risk: if Alpha plays 9→10 in rounds 7-8, we're eliminated. Our only hedge is diplomatic — the message plants the seed that a summit freeze at current rates (75/25 among active nations) serves everyone better than mutual destruction.
